subject: Post-call: EdgeScale token plan & cost options
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Amy Larson <amy.larson@edgescale.com>, Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@edgescale.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: EdgeScale token plan & cost options

Thanks again for your time this morning — good conversation. Summary and agreed next steps below.

Call recap (quick)
- Use case: multi-tenant customer support assistant + morning summaries (mix of short and very long context).
- Expected steady-state: ~1.2B tokens/month; peak windows up to ~2.0B/month during quarterly launches (Q3).
- SLA: <200ms p95 preferred for search/short responses; can tolerate higher for long-form summaries.
- Data: no PHI, but logs retained for 90 days; SOC2 required for production.

Open qualification items we promised to follow up on:
1) Pricing scenarios across: usage-only vs 12-month committed (reserved) capacity; target list to show $/1M tokens for each scenario.
2) Unit economics: expected per-token inference cost before margin, and suggested target price points for EdgeScale (your budget signal helpful).
3) Invoice / procurement path: Tom — you mentioned PO process and 30-day terms; we can prepare a line-item draft invoice.

What we'll send by EOD tomorrow:
- 3 pricing scenarios (attached spreadsheet): pay-as-you-go, 12-month reserved with 20% commit, and a high-commit enterprise plan with custom SLOs. Each includes $/1M token figure.
- A short PDF with cost breakdown and assumptions (tokenization rates, avg tokens per request distribution).
- A draft invoice (line items) for your procurement team to review.

Please confirm if the 1.2B baseline and the 2.0B peak callouts are correct. Also tell us your target $/1M tokens (range) if you have one so we can highlight matching scenarios.

Thanks,
Karthik
From: Amy Larson <amy.larson@edgescale.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@edgescale.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-18T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: EdgeScale token plan & cost options

Thanks Karthik — yes, call notes look right. A couple clarifications from our side:  

- Baseline: 1.2B tokens/month is our internal forecast for months 3–12 post-launch. We expect a ramp: 400M -> 800M -> 1.2B over quarters.
- Peak: spikes to ~2.0B are event-driven (marketing campaigns). Those are short (48–72 hours) but frequent (monthly).
- Token profile: roughly 60% short requests (~50 tokens), 40% long-form (~1,500–2,500 tokens).
- Budget range: finance has signaled a preferrable range of $12k–$20k/month initially — if committed pricing makes unit economics better we can consider that.

Target $/1M tokens: we'd like to see scenarios that get us to $8–$12 per 1M tokens (nett) if possible. If that isn’t realistic, show the closest breakpoints and the tradeoffs (e.g., latency, reserved commit).

On procurement: we use a standard PO process for contracts >$10k/month. Tom handles POs and billing.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Amy

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Amy Larson <amy.larson@edgescale.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@edgescale.com>
Date: 2026-04-19T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: EdgeScale pricing scenarios and cost breakdown (attached)

Hi Amy / Tom — attached are the items we discussed. Quick highlights upfront:

Attachments included:
- edgescale-pricing-scenario.xlsx (three tabs: PAYG, 12mo_reserved_20pct, enterprise_high_commit)
- token-cost-breakdown.pdf (assumptions and per-token math)

Summary (high level)
- Pay-as-you-go (no commit): ~$18 / 1M tokens (estimate) at 1.2B/mo baseline. This is our fully elastic price with no reserved discounts.
- 12-month reserved (20% commit): ~$11.5 / 1M tokens effective across the commit, with burst pricing for >commit. Break-even vs PAYG at ~9 months for your ramp profile.
- Enterprise high-commit (custom): with a 50% commit and SLOs we can get ~ $7.8 / 1M tokens — requires contract and minimum monthly invoice of ~$9k.

Key assumptions (short)
- Tokenization rates: we used your split (60% short @50t, 40% long @1,800t avg).
- Inference ops cost: includes GPU, networking, KV cache hit-rate (we assumed 25% prefix hits), and orchestration overhead.
- Taxes and region uplift excluded from these per-1M figures; invoice will show line items.

Recommended next step: we can prepare a draft invoice for the 12-month reserved scenario (20% commit) to align with your PO threshold and show line-item monthly amounts + one-time setup. Draft invoice attached for procurement review.

[Attachment: edgescale-pricing-scenario.xlsx (spreadsheet, 52KB)]
[Attachment: token-cost-breakdown.pdf (PDF, 18KB)]

Let us know which scenario you prefer; if you want we can also run a sensitivity model for different long-form token averages.

Best,
Vanessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@edgescale.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Amy Larson <amy.larson@edgescale.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-20T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeScale pricing scenarios and cost breakdown (attached)

Thanks Vanessa — the numbers are helpful. A couple of procurement questions before we move to PO:  

1) Can you provide a formal line-item invoice (monthly recurring charge + one-time setup) in PDF so our AP team can validate?
2) We prefer Net 30. Any minimum lead time for cancellations or commit adjustments?
3) For the enterprise high-commit option: does Redwood provide a credits or auto-burst buffer for short spikes (we don't want throttling during campaigns)?

If you can get the draft invoice over today, I’ll route to AP.

— Tom

Subject: Re: EdgeScale pricing scenarios and cost breakdown (attached)

Tom/Amy — sending the draft invoice as Vanessa requested and confirming finance notes:  

- Attached: edgescale-draft-invoice.pdf (line items: monthly reservation fee, burst buffer, one-time setup, estimated tax placeholder).
- Terms: Net 30 OK. For the 12mo_reserved_20pct plan we require a 60-day notice for commit reductions.
- Burst buffer: for enterprise plans we include a configurable burst allowance (30% over commit for up to 72 hours) at no immediate overage — sustained bursts billed at the burst rate in spreadsheet.
- PO processing: our AP team needs a signed SOW + PO referencing deal RDW-ES-2026-042 to map invoices correctly.

[Attachment: edgescale-draft-invoice.pdf (PDF, 14KB)]

If that works, Vanessa — please confirm final scenario and I’ll issue the invoice PDF with invoice number and tax calculations.

Marcus Lin
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
